diagnostic_evidence.quote: we demonstrate that the one-level Schwarz method can achieve robustness with respect to the wave number under specific domain decomposition parameters
Now, for a fixed frequency $k=10$, $L= 1$ and overlap $\delta = 0.1$

We have represented on \cref{fig5:convFactTE-kcomplex} the spectral radius of the iteration matrix for TE-modes (it is the same for TM-modes as previously explained) and the limiting spectrum taking $k = 10 + \imath$.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and contribution list claim the paper shows wavenumber robustness of the one-level method under specific decomposition parameters. No theorem, estimate, or experiment in the source varies k (only k=10 and k=10+i with fixed L, delta are used), and no dependence of max(|a±b|) on k is analysed. The claim is entirely unsupported.

failure_location.quote: We will also show that, under specific domain decomposition parameters, in addition to scalability, the one-level Schwarz method can also achieve robustness with respect of the wavenumber.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the wavenumber-robustness claim from the abstract and contributions, or add an analysis/experiments of the limiting convergence factor as k varies.
issues.overall_effect: One of the four advertised main contributions has no supporting content; the paper establishes limiting-spectrum scalability for fixed k only.
issues.title: Advertised wavenumber robustness is never demonstrated
issues.why_classification: The theoretical results are unaffected, but an advertised contribution must be withdrawn or supplied with new (currently absent) analysis, a non-trivial loss beyond a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Secondly, we aim at showing scalability for discretised Maxwell's equation in a waveguide and decomposition into many subdomains when using different types of transmission conditions.
Numerical experiments confirm that the limiting spectrum effectively predicts practical behavior even with a modest number of subdomains.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper repeatedly announces a second set of numerical results on the discretised Maxwell problem (edge elements, many subdomains), and the abstract claims experiments confirm the prediction of 'practical behavior'. Section 4 contains only evaluations of the spectral radius of the continuous-level modal iteration matrix I^T(r); no discretised Schwarz iteration is reported. The claimed validation of the theory against practical (discrete) behaviour is therefore unsupported.

failure_location.quote: Finally in \Cref{sec:numeric} we present two types of numerical results: first, showing that the limiting spectrum is descriptive for the convergence of the algorithm even in the case of a moderate number of domains and then on the discretised problem using the edge element method.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the announcements of discretised experiments and restate the abstract to say the finite-N spectral radii of the modal iteration matrices approach the limiting spectrum, or add the missing experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the limiting spectrum predicts practical behaviour of the discretised algorithm is unsupported; only consistency of finite-N spectral radii of the modal matrices with their N→∞ limit is shown.
issues.title: Announced discretised (edge-element) scalability experiments are absent
issues.why_classification: Withdrawing the announcement is a local textual correction that leaves all formal results and the continuous-level numerical illustration intact.

issues.failure_explanation: The propositions are stated for any transmission operator satisfying only the diagonalisation assumption eq:op-T-diag, but existence/uniqueness of the amplitudes (and the inverses [M^{l±1,l±1}]^{-1} used in prop:R-ite) require D ≠ 0, which is neither assumed nor proved. It can fail: e.g. λ=0 gives D = 2iκ² sin(β(L+2δ)), vanishing for propagative modes with β(L+2δ) ∈ πZ, so the subdomain problem is not well-posed and the iteration matrices are undefined.

failure_location.quote: Since each subproblem in $\Omega_l$ is well-posed, if we can find $A^{{\rm TE},+,n,l}$ and $A^{{\rm TE},-,n,l}$ such that the BC are verified, then we would prove our result.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis D = (κ+λ)²e^{iβ(L+2δ)} − (λ−κ)²e^{−iβ(L+2δ)} ≠ 0 (well-posedness of the subdomain problems) to the propositions, and note it holds for the impedance and PML operators considered.
issues.overall_effect: As stated for general T, the iteration relations and K^± matrices may be undefined; for the two specific operators actually used (impedance, PML) D ≠ 0 can be verified, so the paper's concrete conclusions survive.
issues.title: Invertibility of the subdomain matrices M^{l,l} (well-posedness) assumed without hypothesis for general T
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis restores the results with no loss for the transmission conditions actually studied.

and with $\kappa = \imath \beta^{\rm TE}$ for TE-modes, $\imath k$ for TEM-modes and $\kappa = \imath \dfrac{k^2}{\beta_{i}^{\rm TM}}$ for TM-modes.
$\lambda_i^{\rm TE} = -\beta^{\rm TE}_i$, $\lambda^{\rm TM}_i = -\frac{k^2}{\beta^{\rm TM}_i}$ and $\lambda^{\rm TEM}_i = -\imath k$

issues.failure_explanation: For ℓ→∞ eq:lambdaPML gives λ^{TE} = −iβ while κ = iβ (similarly for TM, TEM), i.e. λ = −κ, not κ; the proof's own values also drop the factor i. With λ = −κ one has (κ+λ)=0 and b = (−4κ²e^{−iβδ})/(−4κ²e^{−iβ(L+2δ)}) = e^{iβ(L+δ)}, not e^{−iβ(L+δ)}. The stated value would grow for evanescent modes, contradicting the transparency interpretation (with λ=κ, B(E^+) = 2κE^+×n ≠ 0, so outgoing waves would not be absorbed). Only a = 0 (which needs λ² = κ²) and hence the nilpotency conclusion are unaffected.

failure_location.quote: we have $\lambda^{\rm T}_i = \kappa$ and therefore $a^{\rm T}_i = 0$ and $b^{\rm T}_i = e^{-\imath \beta^{\rm T}_i (L+\delta)}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace λ^T_i = κ by λ^T_i = −κ (with the factor i restored in the proof) and b^T_i = e^{−iβ(L+δ)} by b^T_i = e^{iβ(L+δ)}.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit values of λ and b in prop:added-1 are wrong; the nilpotency [I^T(i)]^N = 0 and its interpretation survive.
issues.title: Sign error in the transparent-PML limit: λ = −κ, not κ, so b = e^{iβ(L+δ)}
issues.why_classification: A local sign correction fixes the stated quantities and the main conclusion of the proposition is unchanged.
